note: Art this project did not generate. Every other PNG beside this file is rendered by
tools/sprites and re-rendered pixel for pixel by `npm run sprites:check`; a key declared
here is the exception, and declaring it is what makes it an exception rather than a file
nobody noticed. The owner's call of 2026-09-09 (docs/30, 'Art we did not generate') was
that sprites are commissioned to this project's own spec rather than bought as a pack, so
an authored key is held to the same canvas, the same anchor and the same published bounds
as the rig it stands beside -- `npm run godot:check:authored` is where that is mechanical.
Read by two things, which is the whole point of it being a file rather than a list in code:
tools/sprites/build.py (so --check knows not to try to regenerate it) and
presentation/appearance.gd's `canvas_of` (so the renderer knows its shape). The two-copies
arrangement every other shape table in this project carries -- PAWN_KEYS in Python and in
GDScript, VEHICLE_FOOTPRINTS in both -- is what this replaces for authored art.
`kind` decides which bounds the gate holds a key to:
rig      a body. The published bounds in README.md: height, head, shoulders, clearance,
soles on the bottom row. The eight generated rigs are held to the same numbers
by the same lane, so the spec cannot drift from the art that already meets it.
overlay  a piece of equipment composited onto a body. WORN_LOOK_OK owns its fit.
tile     a tile-sized picture seen from above, centred on its ground point.
`reads` names what draws it -- a content id whose appearance block declares the key. Art
nothing reads is the dead-socket shape this project has paid for twelve times, so the gate
refuses a key that names nothing rather than letting it sit here looking finished.
